- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or neutral (0.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% if recent price drop is steep.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 1–2 days); apply lagged smoothing: subtract 1–3% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling from peak), model overestimates future highs; cap forecast at 1–2 std dev above recent 7-day mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum shifts; if sentiment flips from + to - within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 30–50% for next 5 days.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day forecast; apply downward bias of 3–7% for first 5 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
